title: The Phantom — Lab
description: Experiments in light, depth and place: the Phantom particle toy rebuilt for the graphics card.

intro.title:
A million
points of light.
intro.text: Four small experiments that grew out of the particle toy on the home page — rebuilt for the graphics card, given a body, a camera and somewhere to be.

chapters.title:
Every mark,
a million points.
chapters.text: The original Phantom drew about two thousand dots on a canvas. Here every point is simulated on the graphics card, so the same marks can hold up to a million. Move through them, click to send a shockwave, and open the shutter to watch them as a long exposure would.

chapters.title:
Give the light
a body.
chapters.text: The flat marks are inflated into relief and photographed by a virtual camera that behaves like a real one: the focal lengths of my two lenses, focus that falls off the way a thin lens predicts, and out-of-focus points that open into nine-bladed bokeh.

chapters.title:
Photographs,
with depth.
chapters.text: Each photograph is developed into points and given back its third dimension. From the spot where it was taken it looks exactly like the print; step aside and the scene opens up. Switch to contours to read the picture as a map of equal light.

chapters.title:
Where the light
was.
chapters.text: Every frame was taken somewhere. The atlas starts from the whole planet and descends to the places I photographed, rebuilt from public airborne LiDAR. New York first; more places will follow.

trips.note: The camera clock was on standard time; EXIF times read one hour early. Checked against the sun on p12, which sits on the horizon only when the hour is corrected.

credits: LiDAR: New York City 2017 Topobathymetric survey, distributed by NOAA Digital Coast.
Depth estimates: Depth Anything V2 Small (Apache-2.0), computed offline.
